thread.title: Costco directs most unsold produce to donations and recycling, reports show
thread.title_full: Costco directs most unsold produce to donations and recycling, reports show

author: beaver state news
title: Costco directs most unsold produce to donations and recycling, reports show
text:
A recent report reveals that Costco redirects much of its unsold produce to food banks and other uses rather than sending it to landfills, according to a June 17 discussion on Reddit and reporting by Chowhound. Accounts from volunteers and the company’s own sustainability reports indicate that leftover food is handled through several channels.
Chowhound reported that Costco routes unsold food into four categories: donations, new products, animal feed, and recycling. In a Reddit thread on r/Costco, one volunteer said, “I volunteer several days a week at a food pantry. Costco delivers to us twice a week. They’re incredible!” The company’s 2025 Global Waste Report stated that about 76,000 tons of food were donated to U.S. food programs.
According to the 2025 Annual Sustainability Report cited by Chowhound, produce made up 46.9% of U.S. food donations from Costco within a broader group of items including grains, bread, dairy, and protein—totaling a 74% share for these categories combined.
The issue of food waste in America remains significant; ReFed estimated that the United States generated roughly 70 million tons of surplus food in 2024—representing about 29% of total production. When edible items end up in landfills instead of being consumed or repurposed, resources like water and energy used in their production are also wasted.
Costco said it follows the Environmental Protection Agency’s Wasted Food Scale when determining how best to handle excess inventory. Items unsuitable for donation may be processed into new products or converted into animal feed or biofuel. The company reported diverting 82.8% of its total food waste away from landfills in 2025—surpassing its goal set in 2019.
Reddit users shared additional accounts praising Costco’s donation practices: “I volunteer at a food bank and have seen Costco stuff come in via ‘grocery rescue,'” one poster said. Another wrote: “My partner worked at a wildlife hospital/rehab center and Costco would often donate pallets of fish and veggies to feed eagles, owls, otters.” Some commenters joked about how quickly some purchased produce spoils but generally supported the company’s approach.
